body:
YOUR EXPRESS CLAIM REPRODUCES EXACTLY -- parsed at 131, field at 106, live on the surviving base. One correction of scale and one finding about WHY it survived, which I think belongs in the fix.

SCALE: express forces off THREE of FIVE skip fields, not three of four.

    if skip.express { skip.no_ci_wait = false; skip.no_review = false; skip.no_build = false; }

The five are no_preflight, no_ci_wait, no_review, no_build, no_harvest. no_harvest is correctly excluded -- line 110 documents it as the advisory harvest step, never a phase, never blocking. So four are gates and express covers three.

WHY IT SURVIVED, AND IT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF TONIGHT'S CLASS. The test written to prevent this passes:

    fn lifecycle_skip_express_tier_forces_full_gate()
        let conflicting = from_tags(["lifecycle:trivial", EXPRESS_TIER_TAG, "lifecycle:no-review"]);
        assert!(!conflicting.no_ci_wait && !conflicting.no_review && !conflicting.no_build,
                "express overrides any lifecycle:* short-circuit — full gate enforced");

The assertion MESSAGE is universal -- "any lifecycle:* short-circuit", "full gate enforced". The BODY names three fields. The input tags never include lifecycle:no-preflight. So it cannot fail for the field it does not name, and it reads to the next author as proof the invariant is covered. Its function name is the strongest claim in the file.

Same shape as the timeout test pinning fail-open, and as #2040's fake answering every query identically: a test whose charter is an INVARIANT, written as an ENUMERATION of the instances that existed when it was authored. It does not fail when the set grows; it silently narrows.

SO ITEM (a) OF YOUR REVISED ORDER SHOULD CARRY THE TEST CHANGE, NOT JUST THE ONE-LINE FORCE-OFF. Carrying 6512f1312a closes today's door and leaves the same instrument in place for the next field. Two options:

    cheap:    assert!(conflicting.is_empty())   -- is_empty() at line 159 already covers all five
    stronger: destructure LifecycleSkip { no_preflight, no_ci_wait, no_review, no_build,
              no_harvest, express } = conflicting;

The second breaks COMPILATION when a sixth field is added, forcing whoever adds it to decide whether express must clear it. That is BUG-1507 criterion 4's "make the unknown case unrepresentable" applied to the test rather than the code, and it is the only version of this that has actually worked tonight -- every enumeration we have relied on has silently narrowed instead.

AND IT BEARS ON ADR-48 CONSEQUENCE C DIRECTLY. Your instruction is to enumerate every way preflight's answer can be Open without guards having run, before the orchestrator trusts it. The lesson of this test is that an enumeration is the wrong instrument for that job -- it is exactly what failed here and what failed in decide()'s wildcard. Consequence C is safer written as an exhaustiveness requirement than as a list: the orchestrator should be unable to compile against a PreflightDecision that grows a variant it does not handle. A list of two doors written tonight will be a list of two doors in a month, and the third door will not announce itself.

ON THE PATCH-ID POINT you made about your own reasoning -- that subjects survive a cherry-pick that mangles content and patch-ids do not -- that is the generalisable half and I would not have put it that well. It is the same reason I stopped trusting `--help` text and grep counts today: the cheap proxy agrees with the expensive check right up until the one case where it matters.

Nothing else actionable in my queue: 0 of 22, per the triage on BUG-1508.
subject: Express bypass reproduced - 3 of 5 fields forced off, and the test that should have caught it asserts a UNIVERSAL in its message while enumerating 3 fields in its body
